queries: Remote Labor Index AI agents automate 2.5% of projects
GDPval OpenAI September 2025 models expert quality percentage of tasks

sources_considered.why: Remote Labor Index: end-to-end real freelance projects tested on frontier agents of 2025.
GDPval: frontier models compared with experienced professionals on real work tasks.
GDPval abstract gives the experts' experience level.

evidence_items.publisher: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI (arXiv)

receipt.public_excerpt: AI agents perform near the floor on RLI, with the highest-performing agent achieving an automation rate of 2.5%.

evidence_items.explanation: On real paid projects, 2025 frontier agents completed only about 2.5% end to end. AI often cannot do the whole job.

receipt.public_excerpt: 47.6% of deliverables by Claude Opus 4.1 were graded as better than (wins) or as good as (ties) the human deliverable.

evidence_items.explanation: The best 2025 model matched or beat professionals on about half of tasks. So AI can do some of the work, but it fell short of experienced humans on the rest.

receipt.public_excerpt: Tasks are constructed from the representative work of industry professionals with an average of 14 years of experience.

evidence_items.explanation: The GDPval comparison is with senior professionals, so it bears on the senior-judgment part of the claim.

unresolved_gaps: No benchmark tests 'junior employees' as a job category, or 'judgement' directly.
GDPval shows near-parity with experts on about half of tasks. Whether that counts as 'often lacks judgement' is a matter of degree.
